rawFindings.title: Removed escaping of BOM and EOL from File read operations
rawFindings.explanation: The change removes the use of escapeBOM and escapeEOL utilities which stripped BOM characters and normalized Windows line endings in buffered file content during read operations. This alters existing behavior by no longer normalizing file content on read, which might cause issues where BOM or Windows line endings were previously handled transparently.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore calls to escapeBOM and escapeEOL (previously implemented in escapeContent) in File.prototype.read and File.prototype.readSync methods to preserve content normalization on read.

rawFindings.title: Removal of BOM and EOL escaping breaks behavior
rawFindings.explanation: The change removes the escapeBOM and escapeEOL calls and the related escapeContent function, as well as code in File.prototype.read and File.prototype.readSync that conditionally escapes content by removing BOM and normalizing EOLs. This breaks the escaping behavior for reading files that contain BOM or Windows line endings, possibly causing issues in content processing.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the escapeContent function and calls in File.prototype.read and File.prototype.readSync to maintain BOM and EOL escaping behavior as before.

rawFindings.title: Escape option in File.read and File.readSync is removed causing content to not escape BOM and EOL properly
rawFindings.explanation: The code originally escaped BOM and Windows line endings when reading file content if 'escape' option was true (default). The patch removes the 'escape' option, and disables escapeBOM and escapeEOL usage, returning raw content string without escaping. This changes behavior and can introduce defects in files containing BOM or Windows EOLs, which may break downstream consumers expecting escaped content.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the 'escape' option in wrapReadOptions with default true, and restore the conditional usage of escapeContent in File.prototype.read and readSync to preserve previous behavior.

rawFindings.title: Removed BOM and EOL escaping breaks content correctness
rawFindings.explanation: The removal of the escapeContent function and related calls that escaped BOM and Windows line endings means file.read and file.readSync no longer normalize content by removing BOM or replacing CRLF with LF as before. This may cause unexpected content returned to consumers that relied on the escaping, breaking backward compatibility and potentially leading to bugs in processing file contents.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the calls to escapeContent in read and readSync methods or provide an option to preserve previous escaping behavior to avoid breaking changes for existing code.
